cohort: The study included 27,328 ever-married women aged 15-49 from Bangladesh who had a live birth in the 2 years preceding the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys between 2003 and 2018.
finding: The prevalence of cesarean birth in Bangladesh dramatically increased from 3.99% in 2003-04 to 33.22% in 2017-18, with several socioeconomic and maternal factors significantly influencing this rise.
mod_finding: The prevalence of cesarean birth (CB) in Bangladesh increased from 3.99% to 33.22% between 2003-04 and 2017-18, with maternal age, education, working status, BMI, age at first pregnancy, ANC use, administrative division, and wealth status being significant factors.
cross-section timing: Data collected from Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys between 2003 and 2018.
